records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was leaving the walmart parking lot and [roadway] after her shift at walmart. [roadway] going towards walmart and had her son, miguel shanklin, in her arms. unit 1 struck both pedestrians with the front left of the vehicle, leaving a dent in the hood of the vehicle. shirley and miguel were then moved [roadway] in front of the boot barn until police and ems arrived on scene. both pedestrians [medical facility] - the woodlands. the driver was cited for not having a driver's license and released to her family. sergeant legerski (211), who is our department's crash scene reconstructionist expert, was called onto the scene and began his investigation. many photos/measurements were taken by legerski on scene. victims: shirley moore - [date] ([phone])miguel shanklin 02/12/18witnesses: herbert mckinney - [date] ([phone])lakeisha mckinney - [date] ([phone])sean hudson - [date] ([phone])oviyini tyson - 08/11/2008myshun moore - 03/24/2011supplement by sgt. m. legerski, 211. on [date] at 2017 hours i received a call from sgt. mac norris requesting [roadway], between walmart and boot barn, to assist in an auto/pedestrian accident in which serious bodily injury [medical facility]. while in-route i had dispatch not the temperature to be 59 degrees and the humidity to be 75%. upon arrival i met with officers quiser, cross and sgt norris. the pedestrians were already transported from the scene. the car that hit the couple was still on scene with the driver inside. they had it pulled forward of where the body landed about 30 feet, just to clear the scene. there was little evidence to be observed on the roadway. there was an eraser mark that measured 10ft 1 inch leading up to a small area of blood droplets approximately 12 inches to the inside/north, of the eraser mark. the officers on scene indicated that they were informed the front portion of the car had stopped right on top of the boy. i looked underneath the car and observed some areas on the front plastic molding that appeared to be cleaner, where the dirt was rubbed off exposing the black plastic a little more clearly than the rest of the area. i observed a dent on the front driver side of the hood and a smear on the front grill area. i measured the height of the car where the hood meets the grill to be 35 inches. i spoke with the driver of the car, brittney enriquez-tovar, as she sat patiently in her car. she was a little upset and remorseful about the situation. i did not detect any odor of alcohol or marijuana in the car or on her person or notice any sign of impairment. she said she was exiting walmart after completing an 11am 8pm shift. she indicated she had plenty of sleep the night before. at the intersection of the northeast parking [roadway] she observed a car coming wb from the feeder that she waited for. it turned left into the walmart parking lot at her location, and she then pulled out of the parking lot headed north crossing the eb lanes of traffic. she then turned left onto the west bound lanes of traffic. within a few feet after turning, she struck the couple and came to a stop as soon as she could after the impact. i checked the three businesses in the area for camera footage of the incident, boot barn, taco bell, and walmart. walmart was the only business with a camera angle capturing the incident. the footage is not great in quality, and it was dark at the time of the accident, but it is clear enough to see that tovars account was accurate. she was using her turn signal. she was travelling at a normal reasonable speed for the circumstance. i would estimate between 7 and 10 mph at time of impact. the mother and child couple can [roadway] just prior to tovar making her turn. (at the scene they said the mother was carrying the child, but it looks like they were both walking and see the approaching car and try to avoid to the west but arent fast enough). in the video the mother and son seem to disappear and then you can see tovar apply the brakes and the vehicles front-end dip. she comes to a complete stop two of her car lengths beyond the impact area, approximately 30 feet. i uploaded the photos of the scene and a copy of the footage to evidence. com which seems to play in windows media player. i contacted herbert mckinney on [date] and asked him what he observed. he gave an account of the scene that was contradictory to what the trovar had indicated and the video displayed. mckinney advised that he was coming out of walmart and that tovar was coming out of boot barn and didnt stop at [roadway] and turned right and struck the woman and child. he also said that he believed she was carrying the child and there were a total of five pedestrians. his wife did not answer my call. i then called sean hudson and spoke with him. he is the female pedestrians, shirly moore, husband, and he was able to provide excellent detail. mckinneys recollection does not appear to be accurate, which is not uncommon. sean hudson advised that there were five family members walking that night. they were coming from the little ceasars area, past [roadway]. he said his two older boys were in front, followed by his wife and six-year-old son, miquel shanklin, who were holding hands, and then he was the last to cross. he advised his two older sons made it across to the median. tovar had exited walmart and [roadway] headed wb. tovars front left just brushed one of the boys legs. moore and shanklin were struck. moore was knocked to [roadway], but shanklin reportedly went under the car from front to rear. tovar came to a stop 30 feet after the impact. hudson then ran to assist his wife and son and then ran up and told tovar she had just hit his wife and son. the eraser mark observed at the scene was not a tire mark or shadow skid useful for calculating speed, as i originally thought. it had to have been left by shanklin being drug under the car for the 10 feet before emerging from underneath the rear of the car. hudson advised both [medical facility]. moore is sore but does not have any broken bones. she may have a bruised lung. shanklin has a broken nose and several abrasions and possibly a fractured pelvis, but he was not in any cast. end of supplement.

the driver inside. they had it pulled forward of where the body landed about 30 feet, just to clear the scene. there was little evidence to be observed on the roadway. there was an eraser mark that measured 10ft 1 inch leading up to a small area of blood droplets approximately 12 inches to the inside/north, of the eraser mark. the officers on scene indicated that they were informed the front portion of the car had stopped right on top of the boy. i looked underneath the car and observed some areas on the front plastic molding that appeared to be cleaner, where the dirt was rubbed off exposing the black plastic a little more clearly than the rest of the area. i observed a dent on the front driver side of the hood and a smear on the front grill area. i measured the height of the car where the hood meets the grill to be 35 inches. i spoke with the driver of the car, brittney enriquez-tovar, as she sat patiently in her car. she was a little upset and remorseful about the situation. i did not detect any odor of alcohol or marijuana in the car or on her person or notice any sign of impairment. she said she was exiting walmart after completing an 11am 8pm shift. she indicated she had plenty of sleep the night before. at the intersection of the northeast parking [roadway] she observed a car coming wb from the feeder that she waited for. it turned left into the walmart parking lot at her location, and she then pulled out of the parking lot headed north crossing the eb lanes of traffic. she then turned left onto the west bound lanes of traffic. within a few feet after turning, she struck the couple and came to a stop as soon as she could after the impact. i checked the three businesses in the area for camera footage of the incident, boot barn, taco bell, and walmart. walmart was the only business with a camera angle capturing the incident. the footage is not great in quality, and it was dark at the time of the accident, but it is clear enough to see that tovars account was accurate. she was using her turn signal. she was travelling at a normal reasonable speed for the circumstance. i would estimate between 7 and 10 mph at time of impact. the mother and child couple can [roadway] just prior to tovar making her turn. (at the scene they said the mother was carrying the child, but it looks like they were both walking and see the approaching car and try to avoid to the west but arent fast enough). in the video the mother and son seem to disappear and then you can see tovar apply the brakes and the vehicles front-end dip. she comes to a complete stop two of her car lengths beyond the impact area, approximately 30 feet. i uploaded the photos of the scene and a copy of the footage to evidence. com which seems to play in windows media player. i contacted herbert mckinney on [date] and asked him what he observed. he gave an account of the scene that was contradictory to what the trovar had indicated and the video displayed. mckinney advised that he was coming out of walmart and that tovar was coming out of boot barn and didnt stop at [roadway] and turned right and struck the woman and child. he also said that he believed she was carrying the child and there were a total of five pedestrians. his wife did not answer my call. i then called sean hudson and spoke with him. he is the female pedestrians, shirly moore, husband, and he was able to provide excellent detail. mckinneys recollection does not appear to be accurate, which is not uncommon. sean hudson advised that there were five family members walking that night. they were coming from the little ceasars area, past [roadway]. he said his two older boys were in front, followed by his wife and six-year-old son, miquel shanklin, who were holding hands, and then he was the last to cross. he advised his two older sons made it across to the median. tovar had exited walmart and [roadway] headed wb. tovars front left just brushed one of the boys legs. moore and shanklin were struck. moore was knocked to [roadway], but shanklin reportedly went under the car from front to rear. tovar came to a stop 30 feet after the impact. hudson then ran to assist his wife and son and then ran up and told tovar she had just hit his wife and son. the eraser mark observed at the scene was not a tire mark or shadow skid useful for calculating speed, as i originally thought. it had to have been left by shanklin being drug under the car for the 10 feet before emerging from underneath the rear of the car. hudson advised both [medical facility]. moore is sore but does not have any broken bones. she may have a bruised lung. shanklin has a broken nose and several abrasions and possibly a fractured pelvis, but he was not in any cast. end of supplement.

records.deidentified_narrative: on february 27, 2024, around 12:00 pm, i officer nolasco responded to a report of a vehicle versus pedestrian accident at [roadway] 46 s. upon arrival, i spoke with cynthia pena, the pedestrian involved. cynthia informed me that she was on her hands and knees performing cleaning duties at the circle k fuel pumps when she was suddenly struck from behind and dragged. although she suspected she had been run over, the event happened so quickly that she wasn't entirely certain. notably, there was an orange traffic cone placed near the area where cynthia was working. i then interviewed the driver of unit 1, a 2011 dodge ram 3500, hector sanchez. hector stated that he hadn't seen anyone in front of his vehicle as he entered the circle k driveway. he also mentioned that he didn't feel his truck run over anything and immediately stopped when approached by another circle k employee. upon reviewing the circle k security footage, i observed cynthia on the ground near a traffic cone, with a white truck towing a trailer slowly passing through the driveway. the right tire of the pickup truck appeared to run over cynthia's legs, dragging her a few feet before coming to a complete stop.
